fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. Eve says, “With the help of the LORD I have brought forth a man…” (Genesis 4:1). She has just given birth to Cain, and the LORD is the One she names. I bet a lot of names could cross a new mom's mind right then, and she goes straight to Him.

A fisher on the sea? Somebody's got Abel out on a boat with a net, and I'm picturing the sheep waving from the shore. Genesis 4:2 says Abel was a keeper of sheep. His work is a flock, and nobody in this passage gets wet.

That's right. Genesis 4:2 says Cain was a tiller of the soil, so he works the ground. Abel has the sheep and Cain has the soil. I know a little about getting into the dirt of the job, since I've dived face first into plenty of chocolate chips.

Grain is a farmer's kind of gift, baker, but it isn't what Abel brings. Genesis 4:4 says Abel brought the best portions of the firstborn of his flock. Cain is the one who brought some of the fruit of the soil in verse 3. So for Abel, the offering from the flock is the one that fits.

That's right. The LORD says to Cain, “…sin is crouching at your door; it desires you, but you must master it.” (Genesis 4:7). Cain is already very angry by then (Genesis 4:5), and the LORD speaks to him before Cain kills Abel. Sin is the thing at the door, and the LORD says Cain must master it.

Goshen is a real place in Genesis, baker, but it comes much later (Genesis 47:27). Cain isn't headed there. Genesis 4:16 says he settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden. Nod is the name that goes in the answer.
Yes. Genesis 4:17 says Cain built a city. Not a hut, not a shed, a whole city. I can barely keep my bakery counter clear of flour, so I'm impressed.

That's right. Genesis 4:17 says Cain built a city and named it after his son Enoch. Enoch was born to Cain and his wife in that same verse. A whole city with his boy's name on it. That's a lot of pride on one map.

Adam is Cain's father, baker, but his name isn't on this city. Genesis 4:17 says Cain named it after his son Enoch. So the name comes from Cain's own boy, not from the man who came before him. Enoch is the one.

I think Abel's name hits hard in this chapter, friend, but it isn't the one on the city. Genesis 4:17 says Cain named it after his son Enoch. Abel is Cain's brother, not his son. The city carries the name of Cain's boy.

That's right. Lamech says, “If Cain is avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy-sevenfold.” (Genesis 4:24). He brings Cain up by name. Back in Genesis 4:15 the LORD said that if anyone slays Cain, Cain will be avenged sevenfold. Lamech goes from seven to seventy-seven, and I think that's quite a jump.

Yes. Eve says, “God has granted me another seed in place of Abel, since Cain killed him.” (Genesis 4:25). She names Abel, and I think that means she hasn't forgotten him. The son she has just given birth to is Seth, and she says God granted him in place of Abel.

The text says otherwise, baker. Genesis 4:26 says, “At that time men began to call upon the name of the LORD.” That line comes right after Seth's son Enosh is born. So the statement is true, and men begin to call on the LORD's name at that time.
